phase_web_v2.name: Web Application Testing (OWASP WSTG)
phase_web_v2.description: Coverage tracker for a web application phase, with one item per test case of the OWASP Web Security Testing Guide v4.2 in the guide's own order. Tick each test once it is covered or recorded as not applicable, keep the evidence each item names, and use the API Security Top 10 checklist alongside it for API endpoints.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-01 Search engine discovery for information leakage
items.description:
Finds what search engines and public sources reveal about the target.

  • Indexed pages, caches and archives expose no internal paths or documents.
  • Public code and paste sites hold no keys, configuration or source.
  • Published files carry no metadata naming staff, hosts or versions.

Record: each exposure with URL and date; pass is nothing sensitive retrievable.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-02 Fingerprint the web server
items.description:
Identifies the web server and version to check for known issues.

  • Server and X-Powered-By headers, banners and error pages are generic.
  • Handling of malformed requests agrees with the product identified.
  • The version is vendor-supported with no unpatched advisories.

Record: product, version and how each was inferred; pass is a patched, quiet server.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-03 Review web server metafiles for information leakage
items.description:
Uses metadata files to find hidden paths and understand the site.

  • robots.txt and sitemaps list no sensitive, admin or unpublished paths.
  • security.txt and other .well-known files hold only intended content.
  • Page meta tags and robots directives leak no internal detail.

Record: each file and every disclosed path followed up; pass is nothing useful revealed.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-04 Enumerate applications on the web server
items.description:
Confirms which applications share the in-scope hosts.

  • Non-standard ports, virtual hosts and base paths are enumerated in scope.
  • DNS records and certificate names reveal no unlisted applications.
  • Each application found is agreed as in or out of scope.

Record: host, port, path and virtual host inventory; pass is every application known.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-05 Review web page content for information leakage
items.description:
Checks page source, scripts and metadata for internal information.

  • HTML comments and inline scripts hold no credentials or internal hosts.
  • JavaScript bundles expose no API keys, hidden endpoints or secrets.
  • Source maps and front-end debug files are not served in production.

Record: file, location and item disclosed; pass is nothing sensitive client-side.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-06 Identify application entry points
items.description:
Builds the inventory of inputs that later tests depend on.

  • Parameters, headers, cookies and body fields are logged per function.
  • Hidden fields, JSON, XML, multipart and custom header inputs are included.
  • Responses that set cookies, redirect or change state are noted.

Record: an entry point map per function; complete when every function is exercised.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-07 Map execution paths through the application
items.description:
Maps the main workflows so coverage can be measured.

  • Each role's main workflows are walked end to end, multi-step ones included.
  • Decision points and state changes in each workflow are identified.
  • Automated crawling is reconciled with manual walk-throughs.

Record: the workflow map by role and state; done when each workflow's coverage is known.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-08 Fingerprint the web application framework
items.description:
Identifies frameworks and components so known weaknesses can be checked.

  • Headers, cookie names and markup do not reveal framework versions.
  • Default files and folders of the framework are not exposed.
  • Components are supported with no unpatched published advisories.

Record: each component, version and evidence; pass is patched, quiet components.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-09 Fingerprint the web application
items.description:
Identifies off-the-shelf products behind the site; v4.2 merges this into WSTG-INFO-08.

  • Product, theme and plugin versions are inferred from markup and default files.
  • Default admin paths and install files of the product are absent or protected.
  • Product and plugin versions are supported and patched.

Record: products and versions with evidence; may be shown under WSTG-INFO-08.

items.title: WSTG-INFO-10 Map the application architecture
items.description:
Builds a picture of the components between user and data.

  • Proxies, load balancers, CDNs and WAFs are identified from behaviour.
  • Databases, storage, queues and third-party services are inferred.
  • The hosting model (cloud, serverless, containers, on-premises) is known.

Record: an architecture sketch with evidence per component; it guides later tests.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-01 Network infrastructure configuration
items.description:
Checks the infrastructure supporting the application.

  • Services exposed on application hosts are limited to those required.
  • Web, proxy and application servers are supported and patched.
  • Infrastructure admin interfaces are not public and use no defaults.

Record: components, versions and services; pass is minimal, patched infrastructure.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-02 Application platform configuration
items.description:
Checks the platform for defaults and debug features left in production.

  • Default, sample and test files and applications are removed.
  • Debug modes, verbose errors and developer extensions are disabled.
  • Logs record security events without credentials and are not web-accessible.

Record: each default or debug item and logging notes; pass is a clean platform.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-03 File extension handling for sensitive information
items.description:
Checks which file types the server will serve or execute.

  • Configuration, include, backup and source files cannot be downloaded.
  • Extension rules hold regardless of case or trailing characters.
  • Uploaded files cannot be served with an executable extension.

Record: extensions tried and responses; pass is only intended types served.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-04 Old, backup and unreferenced files
items.description:
Finds forgotten copies that expose source code or data.

  • Backup, renamed and temporary copies of pages and config are not reachable.
  • Archives, dumps and version control folders are absent from the web root.
  • Old pages referenced in archives or scripts are removed.

Record: each file found and its contents; pass is no unreferenced content.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-05 Infrastructure and application admin interfaces
items.description:
Locates admin functions and checks they are not exposed.

  • Admin paths, ports and subdomains have been searched for and listed.
  • Admin interfaces need strong authentication and network or role limits.
  • Altering parameters, cookies or hidden fields cannot reach admin functions.

Record: each interface, exposure and control; pass is restricted admin access.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-06 HTTP methods
items.description:
Checks which HTTP methods are accepted and whether they weaken controls.

  • Only required methods are allowed; TRACE and unused methods are refused.
  • Access decisions are the same for every method and override header.
  • PUT, DELETE and WebDAV methods cannot change server content.

Record: methods per resource; pass is minimal methods, consistently controlled.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-07 HTTP Strict Transport Security
items.description:
Confirms browsers are told to use HTTPS only.

  • Strict-Transport-Security is sent with a max-age of at least a year.
  • includeSubDomains is set where subdomains use HTTPS; preload is considered.
  • HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS before any content or cookie is sent.

Record: the header value per host; pass is a valid, long-lived policy everywhere.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-08 RIA cross-domain policy
items.description:
Checks cross-domain policy files used by rich internet application clients.

  • crossdomain.xml and clientaccesspolicy.xml are absent or name trusted domains.
  • No wildcard grant exposes authenticated content.
  • Policy files on every in-scope host and subdomain are reviewed.

Record: each policy file and its grants; pass is no file or only narrow grants.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-09 File permissions
items.description:
Checks that files and folders follow least privilege.

  • Configuration, key and log files are not world-readable or writable.
  • The web server cannot write to served folders unless required.
  • Executables and scripts cannot be modified by the application account.

Record: permissions reviewed where host access is agreed; pass is least privilege.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-10 Subdomain takeover
items.description:
Finds DNS records pointing at resources the organisation no longer owns.

  • Subdomains are gathered from DNS, certificate logs and archives.
  • CNAME, NS and MX records do not point at deprovisioned cloud or SaaS resources.
  • Expired domains referenced by records are identified.

Record: dangling records and targets (claim nothing unless authorised); pass is none.

items.title: WSTG-CONF-11 Cloud storage
items.description:
Checks access control on storage buckets the application uses.

  • Buckets are identified from URLs, scripts and responses.
  • Anonymous users cannot list, read or write objects unless intended.
  • Signed URLs and authenticated access are narrowly scoped and time-limited.

Record: buckets, permissions and data exposed; pass is private, least-privilege storage.

items.title: WSTG-IDNT-01 Role definitions
items.description:
Documents the roles in use and checks they are separated as intended.

  • Every role and its permissions are listed, with a test account for each.
  • No role is broader than its business need.
  • Changing role values in requests does not switch or assume a role.

Record: the role matrix and accounts used; pass is roles behaving as documented.

items.title: WSTG-IDNT-02 User registration process
items.description:
Checks that self-registration meets business and security needs.

  • Identity checks (email, phone or documents) match the business need.
  • Registration resists bulk automation and duplicate or reserved identities.
  • Users cannot choose their own role or privileges at sign-up.

Record: the flow and weaknesses; pass is verified, rate-limited sign-up with fixed rights.

items.title: WSTG-IDNT-03 Account provisioning process
items.description:
Checks who can create and remove accounts, and of what type.

  • Only authorised roles can provision accounts, never above their own privilege.
  • Provisioning and removal requests are verified and logged.
  • Removed accounts lose access and their sessions end.

Record: the provisioning matrix tested; pass is each role limited as intended.

items.title: WSTG-IDNT-04 Account enumeration and guessable user accounts
items.description:
Checks whether valid accounts can be identified from responses.

  • Login, registration and recovery respond identically for any username.
  • Usernames are not exposed in URLs, profiles or API responses.
  • Account identifiers are not sequential or guessable.

Record: each function compared; pass is indistinguishable responses.

items.title: WSTG-IDNT-05 Weak or unenforced username policy
items.description:
Checks whether the username format makes accounts easy to predict.

  • Usernames do not follow a guessable pattern such as initial and surname or staff number.
  • The username policy is enforced at registration and on change.
  • Errors do not confirm whether a username exists.

Record: the structure and policy observed; pass is unpredictable, enforced usernames.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-01 Credentials sent over an encrypted channel
items.description:
Confirms credentials never travel unencrypted.

  • Login, registration, password change and recovery submit only over HTTPS.
  • Login forms are themselves served over HTTPS with no mixed content.
  • Credentials and tokens never appear in URLs, logs or Referer headers.

Record: transport used per function; pass is HTTPS everywhere.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-02 Default credentials
items.description:
Checks for vendor defaults and predictable initial credentials.

  • Built-in and admin accounts reject vendor default passwords.
  • New accounts are not issued a default or patterned password.
  • Test, demo and service accounts are removed or strongly secured.

Record: accounts tried within agreed limits; pass is no default credential works.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-03 Weak lockout mechanism
items.description:
Checks that failed logins are throttled without enabling denial of service.

  • Lockout or throttling starts after a small, documented number of failures.
  • It covers every login route, APIs and MFA steps included.
  • Unlocking relies on time or a verified process an attacker cannot trigger.

Record: thresholds and unlock behaviour on test accounts; pass is consistent throttling.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-04 Authentication schema bypass
items.description:
Checks that every protected resource enforces authentication.

  • Protected pages and API endpoints refuse direct unauthenticated requests.
  • Altering parameters, cookies or step order in login grants no access.
  • Authentication state is decided server-side, not from client values.

Record: each attempt and response; pass is consistent server-side enforcement.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-05 Vulnerable remember password
items.description:
Checks 'remember me' and stored-password features for credential exposure.

  • Remember-me tokens are random, server-validated, expiring and credential-free.
  • No password is stored in cookies or browser storage.
  • A remembered login still needs re-authentication for sensitive actions.

Record: token format, lifetime and storage; pass is no credential kept client-side.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-06 Browser cache weaknesses
items.description:
Checks that sensitive pages are not kept in the browser cache or history.

  • Authenticated pages with sensitive data send Cache-Control: no-store.
  • After logout, the back button does not redisplay sensitive pages.
  • Sensitive data is not placed in URLs that persist in history.

Record: headers per page and back-button results; pass is nothing sensitive retained.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-07 Weak password policy
items.description:
Checks how well the password rules resist guessing.

  • A minimum length of at least eight is enforced and long passphrases are accepted.
  • Common and breached passwords are rejected.
  • Rules are enforced server-side at registration, change and reset.

Record: the effective policy; pass is in line with NIST SP 800-63B or ASVS V6.2.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-08 Weak security questions and answers
items.description:
Checks knowledge-based questions used for recovery or login.

  • Answers cannot be found publicly, guessed or taken from social media.
  • Answer attempts are rate limited.
  • Questions are never the only factor for recovery.

Record: questions offered and attempt limits; pass is no reliance on weak questions.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-09 Weak password change or reset functions
items.description:
Checks that password change and reset cannot enable account takeover.

  • Change needs the current password; reset tokens are random and single-use.
  • Reset links are bound to the account and ignore Host header changes.
  • Reset reveals no account existence and does not bypass MFA.

Record: token properties and flow; pass is a reset only the owner can complete.

items.title: WSTG-ATHN-10 Weaker authentication in alternative channels
items.description:
Checks that mobile apps, APIs and legacy sites are as strong as the main login.

  • All authentication channels and their controls have been listed.
  • Each channel applies the same password policy, lockout and MFA.
  • No alternative channel exposes functions with weaker authentication.

Record: channels and controls compared; pass is equal strength across channels.

items.title: WSTG-ATHZ-01 Directory traversal and file inclusion
items.description:
Checks that inputs naming files or paths stay within intended locations.

  • Parameters, cookies and headers referencing files or templates are identified.
  • Path manipulation, encoded separators included, reaches no other files.
  • File access uses an allowlist or index, not user-supplied paths.

Record: each input and result; pass is no access beyond intended files.

items.title: WSTG-ATHZ-02 Authorisation schema bypass
items.description:
Checks that each role reaches only the functions and data it should.

  • Every function is requested as each role and anonymously, against the matrix.
  • Other users' data at the same level cannot be reached.
  • Controls are enforced server-side, not just by hiding links or buttons.

Record: the access matrix tested; pass is every request matching intended permissions.

items.title: WSTG-ATHZ-03 Privilege escalation
items.description:
Checks whether users can raise their own privileges.

  • Role or group values in requests, cookies or tokens cannot be altered to gain access.
  • Profile and account updates ignore privilege fields.
  • Higher-role functions refuse lower-privileged sessions.

Record: each manipulation point and result; pass is no privilege change from the client side.

items.title: WSTG-ATHZ-04 Insecure direct object references
items.description:
Checks that objects referenced by ID are reachable only by those entitled.

  • IDs in paths, parameters and bodies are swapped between two same-role users.
  • Read, update and delete operations all check ownership.
  • Unpredictable identifiers are not the only control.

Record: each object type and operation tested; pass is ownership enforced on every access.

items.title: WSTG-SESS-01 Session management schema
items.description:
Analyses how session tokens are created and whether they can be predicted.

  • Tokens are long and random; a sample shows no pattern.
  • Tokens carry no readable or editable user data unless signed and verified.
  • Each new session receives a new token.

Record: token samples, structure and analysis; pass is unpredictable, tamper-proof tokens.

items.title: WSTG-SESS-02 Cookie attributes
items.description:
Checks that cookie security attributes are set appropriately.

  • Session and sensitive cookies set Secure, HttpOnly and a fitting SameSite value.
  • Domain and Path are narrow; __Host- prefixes are used where suitable.
  • Session cookies are not persistent unless needed.

Record: each cookie and its attributes; pass is every sensitive cookie flagged and scoped.

items.title: WSTG-SESS-03 Session fixation
items.description:
Checks that a token known before login cannot be used after it.

  • A new token is issued at login and at any privilege change.
  • Tokens supplied before authentication are discarded.
  • Tokens cannot be set through URL parameters.

Record: tokens before and after login; pass is a fresh token on each authentication.

items.title: WSTG-SESS-04 Exposed session variables
items.description:
Checks that session tokens stay protected wherever they travel.

  • Tokens go only over HTTPS and never in URLs or GET parameters.
  • Responses carrying tokens are not cached by browsers or proxies.
  • Tokens do not appear in logs, Referer headers or error pages.

Record: where tokens appear; pass is tokens confined to protected channels.

items.title: WSTG-SESS-05 Cross-site request forgery
items.description:
Checks whether state-changing requests can be triggered from another site.

  • State changes need an anti-forgery token, custom header or strict SameSite.
  • Tokens are session-bound and checked server-side, JSON endpoints included.
  • No state change is possible through GET.

Record: each state-changing function and its protection; pass is nothing forgeable.

items.title: WSTG-SESS-06 Logout functionality
items.description:
Checks that logout ends the session on the server.

  • Logout is available from every authenticated page.
  • After logout, a replayed token is rejected server-side.
  • Single sign-on logout also ends identity provider sessions where intended.

Record: requests replayed after logout; pass is immediate server-side invalidation.

items.title: WSTG-SESS-07 Session timeout
items.description:
Checks idle and absolute session lifetimes.

  • An idle timeout ends sessions after a period suited to the risk.
  • An absolute timeout forces re-authentication regardless of activity.
  • Expiry is enforced server-side, not only in the browser.

Record: timeouts with timestamps; pass is behaviour matching the documented policy.

items.title: WSTG-SESS-08 Session puzzling
items.description:
Checks whether one session variable is reused unsafely across functions.

  • Values set by one flow, such as password reset, cannot satisfy checks in another.
  • Part-completed flows do not leave the session authenticated or privileged.
  • Each function validates the session values it relies on.

Record: the variables and flows involved; pass is no cross-flow reuse of session state.

items.title: WSTG-SESS-09 Session hijacking
items.description:
Checks how easily a session cookie could be captured and reused.

  • Session cookies are never sent over HTTP, even on a first visit before redirect.
  • HSTS and the Secure attribute together prevent cleartext exposure.
  • Sensitive actions need re-authentication, limiting a stolen session's value.

Record: exposure routes; pass is no route for a session cookie to leave HTTPS.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-01 Reflected cross-site scripting
items.description:
Checks that input reflected in responses is encoded for its context.

  • Every reflected parameter, header and path segment has been identified.
  • Reflected data is encoded for its HTML, attribute, script or URL context.
  • A Content-Security-Policy limits script execution as a second layer.

Record: each reflection point, context and outcome; pass is correct encoding everywhere.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-02 Stored cross-site scripting
items.description:
Checks that stored input is encoded wherever it is later shown.

  • Stored fields such as profiles, comments and file names are traced to every view.
  • Output is encoded for its context, admin and reporting views included.
  • Rich text is sanitised with a maintained library.

Record: each storage point and display location; pass is safe rendering in every view.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-03 HTTP verb tampering
items.description:
Checks that access control ignores the HTTP method; v4.2 merges this into WSTG-CONF-06.

  • Protected resources give one decision for GET, POST, HEAD and arbitrary methods.
  • Method-override headers and parameters are ignored or equally controlled.
  • Server and framework method restrictions agree.

Record: methods tried per resource; may be shown under WSTG-CONF-06.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-04 HTTP parameter pollution
items.description:
Checks how duplicated parameters are handled across components.

  • The precedence each tier gives duplicate parameters is known.
  • Duplicates cannot slip past validation, filters or access checks.
  • Front-end and back-end components read parameters the same way.

Record: behaviour per endpoint; pass is consistent handling no duplicate can subvert.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-05 SQL injection
items.description:
Checks that input reaching database queries cannot change their structure.

  • All inputs are assessed, including headers, cookies and sort fields.
  • Responses, errors and timing show no change in query logic as input varies.
  • NoSQL, ORM and client-side databases, the guide's subsections, are covered.

Record: each input and result; pass is parameterised queries that no input can alter.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-06 LDAP injection
items.description:
Checks that input used in directory searches cannot alter the filter.

  • Inputs feeding directory lookups, such as login or people search, are identified.
  • Filter special characters are escaped or rejected.
  • No altered results, errors or logins follow from changed filters.

Record: inputs tested and responses; pass is no change to directory query logic.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-07 XML injection
items.description:
Checks XML parsing and whether input can alter documents or load entities.

  • Parsers reject DTDs and external entities (XXE).
  • Input inserted into XML is encoded so it cannot add or change elements.
  • SOAP endpoints and XML-based uploads such as SVG and DOCX are included.

Record: endpoints, parser behaviour and impact; pass is safe parsing and no structure change.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-08 Server-side include injection
items.description:
Checks whether server-side include directives in input are processed.

  • The server's support for server-side includes is established.
  • Input reflected in pages or written to files is never run as a directive.
  • SSI processing is disabled where not needed.

Record: inputs tested and server behaviour; pass is directives treated as plain text.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-09 XPath injection
items.description:
Checks that input used in XPath queries cannot change them.

  • Functions querying XML data stores are identified.
  • Query special characters are escaped or the query is precompiled.
  • Errors and result differences show no change in query logic.

Record: inputs and responses; pass is no input altering XPath structure.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-10 IMAP and SMTP injection
items.description:
Checks that input passed to mail servers cannot add commands or headers.

  • Webmail, contact and notification features that reach mail servers are identified.
  • Line breaks and protocol characters are rejected or encoded.
  • Recipients, headers and bodies cannot be added or altered.

Record: inputs tested and server responses; pass is no injected mail command or header.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-11 Code injection
items.description:
Checks whether input can be evaluated as code, including through file inclusion.

  • Functions that evaluate, compile or include input are identified.
  • Input never reaches dynamic evaluation without strict validation.
  • Local and remote file inclusion, the guide's subsections, are refused.

Record: inputs tested and outcomes; pass is no input executed as code.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-12 Command injection
items.description:
Checks that input passed to OS commands cannot add or change commands.

  • Features likely to call the OS, such as conversion or archiving, are identified.
  • Shell metacharacters have no effect, even where output is not returned.
  • Commands run without a shell and with fixed arguments.

Record: inputs, observations and impact; pass is no command execution from input.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-13 Format string injection
items.description:
Checks whether format specifiers in input are interpreted.

  • Inputs reaching logging, formatting or native code are identified.
  • Specifiers in input cause no crash, memory disclosure or altered output.
  • Format strings are fixed in code, never taken from input.

Record: inputs tested and behaviour; pass is specifiers treated as literal text.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-14 Incubated vulnerabilities
items.description:
Checks for stored input that only takes effect later, in another context.

  • Stored data later handled by admins, other users or batch jobs is identified.
  • Stored and uploaded content stays safe when recalled, exported or rendered.
  • Delayed effects are watched for over a suitable period.

Record: storage point, recall path and impact; pass is safe handling at recall.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-15 HTTP splitting and smuggling
items.description:
Checks for header injection and whether components agree on request boundaries.

  • CR and LF characters in input never reach response headers.
  • Front-end and back-end agree on Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding handling.
  • Ambiguous requests are rejected by the first component.

Record: requests tested with care on shared systems; pass is neither issue present.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-16 HTTP incoming requests
items.description:
Observes traffic server-side to find requests invisible from the client.

  • Server or network monitoring is arranged with the client where in scope.
  • Background calls to third parties and internal services are identified.
  • No unexpected or unencrypted request carries sensitive data.

Record: unexpected requests and content; pass is only expected, protected traffic.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-17 Host header injection
items.description:
Checks whether the application trusts the Host and forwarding headers.

  • Absolute links, reset URLs and redirects are not built from the supplied Host.
  • X-Forwarded-Host and similar headers cannot override the host.
  • Caches do not store responses generated for a manipulated host.

Record: headers tested and effects; pass is a fixed, configured host name used throughout.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-18 Server-side template injection
items.description:
Checks whether input is evaluated by a server-side template engine.

  • Inputs rendered through templates, such as emails, PDFs and previews, are identified.
  • Template expressions in input are not evaluated.
  • Templates are never built from input; sandboxing is used where needed.

Record: inputs, engine identified and outcome; pass is input rendered as data only.

items.title: WSTG-INPV-19 Server-side request forgery
items.description:
Checks whether the server can be made to request unintended destinations.

  • URL-fetching features such as webhooks, imports and previews are listed.
  • Internal, loopback and metadata addresses are refused, after redirects too.
  • Destination checks use an allowlist and resist alternative address encodings.

Record: each feature and destinations reached; pass is only intended destinations.

items.title: WSTG-ERRH-01 Improper error handling
items.description:
Checks that errors are handled safely and reveal nothing useful.

  • Malformed input, missing parameters and invalid paths produce generic messages.
  • Errors expose no stack traces, queries, file paths or versions.
  • Error states fail closed and skip no security check.

Record: requests that caused errors and their output; pass is generic, consistent errors.

items.title: WSTG-ERRH-02 Stack traces
items.description:
Checks that no request yields a stack trace; v4.2 merges this into WSTG-ERRH-01.

  • Unexpected types, encodings and lengths produce no stack trace.
  • Framework debug and exception pages are disabled in production.
  • API and background endpoints also return generic errors.

Record: any trace observed; may be shown under WSTG-ERRH-01.

items.title: WSTG-CRYP-01 Weak transport layer security
items.description:
Checks the TLS configuration of every in-scope service.

  • Only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 are enabled, with strong suites and forward secrecy.
  • Certificates are valid, trusted, match the host and use strong keys and signatures.
  • No content, form or redirect falls back to HTTP.

Record: protocols, suites and certificates per host; pass is no weak option offered.

items.title: WSTG-CRYP-02 Padding oracle
items.description:
Checks whether encrypted values reveal padding validity via errors or timing.

  • Block-cipher encrypted tokens, cookies or parameters are identified.
  • Altered values give one generic response, with no padding-specific difference.
  • Integrity is protected by authenticated encryption or a MAC.

Record: values tested and differences; pass is no distinguishable padding behaviour.

items.title: WSTG-CRYP-03 Sensitive information sent over unencrypted channels
items.description:
Checks every channel carrying sensitive data for encryption.

  • No credentials, tokens or personal data travel over HTTP or other cleartext protocols.
  • HTTPS pages load no resources over HTTP.
  • Back-end and third-party connections seen during testing are encrypted.

Record: each channel and the data observed; pass is all sensitive data encrypted in transit.

items.title: WSTG-CRYP-04 Weak encryption
items.description:
Checks for weak algorithms, modes and key handling.

  • No MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4 or ECB mode protects sensitive data.
  • Passwords are stored with a salted, slow hash, where this can be verified.
  • Keys, IVs and random values are not hard-coded, reused or predictable.

Record: algorithms observed and where; pass is current algorithms and sound key handling.

items.title: WSTG-BUSL-01 Business logic data validation
items.description:
Checks that the server validates data against business rules, not just format.

  • Format-valid but illogical values, such as negative quantities, are refused.
  • Client-side checks are repeated on the server.
  • Data cannot be changed between steps of a flow.

Record: each rule tested and outcome; pass is server-side enforcement of business rules.

items.title: WSTG-BUSL-02 Ability to forge requests
items.description:
Checks whether hidden or predictable parameters bypass the intended workflow.

  • Hidden fields, debug flags and unused parameters have been identified.
  • Adding or changing parameters unlocks no features, discounts or other data.
  • Requests the normal flow never produces are rejected where it matters.

Record: parameters altered and effects; pass is no unintended function reachable.

items.title: WSTG-BUSL-03 Integrity checks
items.description:
Checks that data cannot be changed where the business logic says it should not be.

  • Server-calculated fields such as prices, totals and roles cannot be set.
  • Data passed between components is integrity-protected where it matters.
  • Audit records cannot be altered by users.

Record: fields tested and results; pass is that only authorised changes succeed.

items.title: WSTG-BUSL-04 Process timing
items.description:
Checks whether timing leaks information or can be abused.

  • Response times do not reveal valid accounts, codes or internal states.
  • Time-limited operations cannot be extended or reused beyond their window.
  • Parallel requests cannot exploit races in balances, stock or vouchers.

Record: timings and concurrency results; pass is no exploitable timing behaviour.

items.title: WSTG-BUSL-05 Limits on how often a function can be used
items.description:
Checks that limits on repeat use of a function are enforced.

  • Limited functions, such as vouchers, votes or trials, are identified.
  • Limits hold server-side per user and globally, under parallel requests too.
  • New sessions, accounts or parameter changes do not reset limits.

Record: each limit and its enforcement; pass is limits holding under parallel use.

items.title: WSTG-BUSL-06 Circumvention of workflows
items.description:
Checks that multi-step flows must be completed in order.

  • Steps cannot be skipped, repeated or reordered by calling later requests directly.
  • Each step confirms earlier steps completed for the same user and transaction.
  • Abandoned or failed flows leave no usable partial state.

Record: flows tested and deviations; pass is sequencing enforced on the server.

items.title: WSTG-BUSL-07 Defences against application misuse
items.description:
Checks whether the application notices and reacts to misuse seen during testing.

  • Invalid input, forced browsing and tampering trigger alerts or throttling.
  • Responses escalate as misuse continues.
  • The client confirms whether test activity was detected and logged.

Record: activity and reactions seen; pass is detection with a proportionate response.

items.title: WSTG-BUSL-08 Upload of unexpected file types
items.description:
Checks that uploads accept only the file types the business needs.

  • Allowed types are enforced server-side by extension and content, not only MIME type.
  • Batch and archive uploads apply the same rules.
  • Accepted files cannot be served or processed as another type.

Record: types tried and results; pass is strict server-side type enforcement.

items.title: WSTG-BUSL-09 Upload of malicious files
items.description:
Checks how uploads are processed and whether harmful content is caught.

  • Uploads are malware-scanned and stored or served so they cannot execute.
  • Archives and documents are checked for size, expansion and embedded content.
  • Harmless standard test files such as EICAR are detected.

Record: files tried and processing seen; pass is harmful content rejected or neutralised.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-01 DOM-based cross-site scripting
items.description:
Checks client code that writes attacker-influenced data into the page.

  • Sources such as location, hash and postMessage are traced to sinks like innerHTML.
  • Data reaching sinks is encoded or uses safe APIs such as textContent.
  • Trusted Types or a strict CSP restrict dangerous sinks.

Record: source-to-sink paths and outcomes; pass is no untrusted data at unsafe sinks.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-02 JavaScript execution
items.description:
Checks whether input can run as JavaScript in the page.

  • Inputs written into script blocks, event handlers or script URLs are identified.
  • Client code neither navigates to nor evaluates strings taken from input.
  • Script-bearing URL schemes are refused wherever URLs are accepted.

Record: injection points and outcomes; pass is no input executing as script.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-03 HTML injection
items.description:
Checks whether input can add markup to the page even where script is blocked.

  • Input inserted into the DOM is encoded or uses safe text APIs.
  • Injected markup cannot create forms, links or content that mislead users.
  • Rich-text sanitisers are current and strictly configured.

Record: points and effects; pass is no user-controlled markup rendered.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-04 Client-side URL redirect
items.description:
Checks whether client code can be made to redirect users to untrusted sites.

  • Parameters and fragments used for navigation in client code are identified.
  • Redirect targets are limited to an allowlist or relative paths.
  • Script-bearing URL schemes are refused.

Record: redirect inputs and destinations reached; pass is redirects limited to trusted locations.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-05 CSS injection
items.description:
Checks whether input can inject style rules into the page.

  • Inputs placed in style attributes, style blocks or stylesheets are identified.
  • Injected styles cannot read page data or restyle the page to mislead.
  • CSS values are validated against an allowlist.

Record: points and effects; pass is no user-controlled CSS.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-06 Client-side resource manipulation
items.description:
Checks whether input controls which resources the page loads.

  • Inputs that set script, frame, image or XHR URLs are identified.
  • Resource URLs are restricted to trusted origins.
  • Content-Security-Policy limits where resources can load from.

Record: points and resources loaded; pass is no user control over resource locations.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-07 Cross-origin resource sharing
items.description:
Checks the CORS policy on each endpoint.

  • Access-Control-Allow-Origin is not reflected from any origin or set to null.
  • Credentials are allowed only for specific trusted origins.
  • Origin checks reject lookalike domains and unexpected subdomains.

Record: origins tried and headers returned; pass is a strict, credential-safe allowlist.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-08 Cross-site flashing
items.description:
Checks any Flash content for unsafe parameter handling; now largely historical.

  • Any SWF files served by the application are identified.
  • Flash content is retired, since current browsers no longer run it.
  • Where present, FlashVars and URL parameters do not reach unsafe methods.

Record: SWF files found, or none; pass is no Flash content served.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-09 Clickjacking
items.description:
Checks whether pages can be framed by other sites.

  • Sensitive pages send CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options that block framing.
  • Protection covers every sensitive page and state-changing view.
  • Frame-busting scripts are not relied on alone.

Record: headers per page and framing results; pass is framing refused to untrusted origins.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-10 WebSockets
items.description:
Checks WebSocket connections with the same rigour as HTTP endpoints.

  • Connections use WSS and the handshake checks the Origin header.
  • Messages are authenticated, authorised and validated like HTTP requests.
  • Connection and message limits prevent resource exhaustion.

Record: endpoints, handshake and message results; pass is controls equal to HTTP.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-11 Web messaging
items.description:
Checks postMessage communication between windows and frames.

  • Listeners check the sender's origin against an exact allowlist.
  • Received data is validated and kept away from unsafe sinks.
  • Outgoing messages name a target origin rather than a wildcard.

Record: listeners and senders reviewed; pass is strict origin checks and safe handling.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-12 Browser storage
items.description:
Checks what the application keeps in browser storage.

  • Web storage, IndexedDB and cookies hold no sensitive data beyond session tokens.
  • Stored data is cleared at logout.
  • Values read back from storage are kept away from unsafe sinks.

Record: keys and values stored; pass is no sensitive data persisted client-side.

items.title: WSTG-CLNT-13 Cross-site script inclusion
items.description:
Checks whether authenticated data can be included cross-origin as script.

  • Responses with sensitive data are not valid script; there is no JSONP.
  • JSON and script resources use correct content types with nosniff.
  • SameSite cookies or Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy limit cross-site inclusion.

Record: resources reviewed and data exposed; pass is nothing sensitive includable.

items.title: WSTG-APIT-01 GraphQL
items.description:
Checks GraphQL configuration, input handling and access control.

  • Introspection and debug output are off in production unless the API is public.
  • Query depth, cost, batching and alias limits are enforced.
  • Resolvers authorise every object and field and validate arguments.

Record: endpoints, schema exposure and findings; pass is per-field access control.

phase_internal_v2.name: Internal Infrastructure Review
phase_internal_v2.description: Coverage tracker for an internal infrastructure test, in the order a tester usually works: scope and discovery, segmentation, management services, patching, legacy protocols, name resolution and relay, credentials, databases, virtualisation, backup and storage, network and embedded devices, port access control, then endpoint and logging observations. Tick each item once covered or recorded as not applicable, and attach the Active Directory Security Review checklist for the directory itself.

items.title: Scope, rules of engagement and test constraints
items.description:
Confirms what may be tested, from where and how, so later checks stay authorised and fragile systems are handled safely.

  • In-scope ranges and exclusions match the signed scope, including third-party and shared systems.
  • Testing windows, rate limits and any ban on lockout or disruption are agreed.
  • Fragile systems (OT, medical, legacy) are flagged for gentler testing.
  • An out-of-hours contact and stop conditions exist.

Record: scope reference, exclusions, contacts and constraints; passing means no host is tested without a matching scope entry.

items.title: Starting position and access recorded
items.description:
Fixes the vantage point behind each result, because reachability and segmentation findings only make sense relative to it.

  • The connection point, VLAN, address assignment and whether network access control admitted the device are noted.
  • Any supplied account or build is recorded with its privilege level.
  • Key checks are repeated from each further position the scope names (user, server, management, guest).

Record: each position with date, address, VLAN and account, so every finding traces to where it was seen.

items.title: Host discovery across in-scope ranges
items.description:
Establishes which hosts are live, since gaps here silently shrink the test (NIST SP 800-115 section 4.1).

  • Several methods are combined, so hosts that ignore ICMP or filter common ports are still found.
  • Passive observation (ARP, broadcast and multicast traffic) is compared with active results.
  • Live hosts are reconciled with the asset register, DHCP and DNS data.
  • Filtered ranges are noted, not assumed empty.

Record: live hosts per range, methods and gaps; passing means coverage matches the expected estate.

items.title: Service and version inventory (TCP and UDP)
items.description:
Builds the inventory every later check works from (NIST SP 800-115 section 4.2).

  • All TCP ports are covered on in-scope hosts, not only common ones.
  • UDP covers at least DNS, SNMP, NTP, TFTP, IPMI and NetBIOS.
  • Services and versions are identified by protocol behaviour, not port number alone.
  • Unexpected services and unknown hosts go to the client to confirm ownership.

Record: host, port, protocol, service, version and scan date; passing means every listening service is known and owned.

items.title: Segmentation between network zones
items.description:
Tests whether zones believed separate really are; weak internal filtering lets one compromised workstation reach everything.

  • A matrix shows which zones (user, server, management, OT, payment, guest) reach which ports in others.
  • Management, database and backup ports are unreachable from user and guest zones.
  • Dual-homed hosts and jump servers do not bridge zones unintentionally.

Record: the matrix with source, destination, port and result, against the documented design; passing means only justified flows exist.

items.title: Firewall and router ruleset review
items.description:
Where rule exports are supplied, checks the rules themselves rather than inferring them from probes (NIST SP 800-115 section 3.3).

  • Rules deny by default, and broad source, destination or service objects are justified.
  • Every rule is still needed; temporary and unused rules are gone.
  • Specific rules sit above general ones and none lets traffic bypass another control.
  • Each permit rule has an owner and a business reason.

Record: rule identifiers of concern and why; passing means every permit rule is specific, owned and current.

items.title: Outbound filtering from internal zones
items.description:
Shows whether internal hosts can reach the internet directly, which governs how easily data or control traffic could leave.

  • Servers cannot open arbitrary outbound connections.
  • User zones reach the internet only through the intended proxy or gateway.
  • Outbound DNS is limited to the internal resolvers.
  • Outbound SMB, RDP and SSH are blocked at the perimeter.

Record: ports and destinations reachable from each zone; passing means egress is limited to defined services.

items.title: Layer 2 protections on access switches
items.description:
Checks whether a device on a user port could impersonate the gateway or DHCP server and so intercept neighbours' traffic. Test only where the rules of engagement allow.

  • DHCP snooping and dynamic ARP inspection, or equivalents, are on for user VLANs.
  • Access ports do not negotiate trunking, and the native VLAN is not a user or management VLAN.
  • Port security or network access control limits devices per port.

Record: switch behaviour per VLAN; passing means spoofed gateway or DHCP responses are not accepted.

items.title: Remote administration services (RDP, SSH, WinRM, VNC)
items.description:
Remote administration services are the usual route for lateral movement, so who can reach them and how they authenticate matters most.

  • RDP, WinRM, SSH and VNC are reachable only from management zones or jump hosts.
  • RDP requires Network Level Authentication; VNC always requires authentication.
  • SSH offers no deprecated algorithms and refuses root login by password.

Record: each service, where it is reachable from and its authentication settings; passing means admin services face admin sources only.

items.title: Out-of-band management controllers (BMC and IPMI)
items.description:
Management controllers give power and console control below the operating system, so their exposure undermines everything above.

  • BMC web, SSH and IPMI interfaces sit on a dedicated management network.
  • IPMI 2.0 is disabled where unneeded, as its RAKP exchange discloses a password-derived hash for any valid user.
  • Cipher suite zero is refused, default accounts are changed and firmware is current.

Record: controllers, placement, protocols and firmware; passing means they are reachable only from the management network.

items.title: Web-based administration consoles
items.description:
Internal consoles for application servers, monitoring, build and deployment tools and appliances are often weaker than internet-facing ones, and many can run code.

  • Every console requires authentication; none expose dashboards, job runners or script consoles anonymously.
  • Logins use HTTPS and refuse default or shared accounts.
  • Consoles that can run code or deploy software face admin zones only.

Record: URL, product, version and access obtained; passing means authenticated, encrypted and admin-only.

items.title: Patch levels against known exploited vulnerabilities
items.description:
Prioritises missing patches that attackers are known to use, rather than raw scanner counts (NIST SP 800-115 section 4.3).

  • Authenticated or agent-based results are used where in scope.
  • Versions are checked against vendor advisories and the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalogue.
  • Findings rest on version evidence or safe checks, not a scanner rating alone.
  • Patch age shows whether patching works.

Record: host, product, version, missing update, KEV status and evidence; passing means no KEV-listed issue is outstanding.

items.title: Unsupported operating systems and software
items.description:
Identifies systems that no longer receive security updates; patching cannot fix them, so they need isolation or replacement.

  • Operating systems, databases, middleware and appliance firmware past vendor end of support are listed.
  • Any extended support contract is confirmed rather than assumed.
  • Unsupported systems that must stay are isolated, with filtered access and extra monitoring.

Record: host, product, version and end-of-support date; passing means none remain, or each is isolated under a recorded exception.

items.title: SMB version 1, null sessions and guest access
items.description:
SMB version 1 lacks modern protections and has a history of wormable flaws, and anonymous SMB access leaks users, groups and shares to anyone on the network.

  • No host accepts or offers SMB version 1.
  • Anonymous (null session) connections cannot enumerate users, groups, shares or policy.
  • Guest access to shares is disabled on servers and NAS devices.

Record: hosts accepting SMB version 1, null sessions or guest access, with what was disclosed; passing means none do.

items.title: Cleartext management and file transfer protocols
items.description:
Cleartext protocols expose credentials and data to anyone on the path; passive capture reveals them (NIST SP 800-115 section 3.5).

  • Telnet, FTP, TFTP, rlogin and rsh are absent, or justified and isolated.
  • Admin web interfaces use HTTPS, not HTTP.
  • Directory, database and mail services encrypt authentication.
  • Where capture is authorised, credentials seen in clear are noted but not retained.

Record: host, protocol and what it carries; passing means credentials never cross the network unencrypted.

items.title: SNMP versions and community strings
items.description:
SNMP can disclose configuration, interfaces, routes, accounts and running software, and write access can change device settings.

  • SNMP v1 and v2c are unused, or limited by source address with non-default, hard-to-guess community strings.
  • No read-write community exists where it is not needed.
  • SNMPv3 uses authentication and privacy (authPriv) with current algorithms.

Record: host, version, access level and what was readable; passing means SNMPv3 authPriv from management stations only.

items.title: Encryption on internal services
items.description:
Internal services with weak or no transport encryption let anyone positioned on the network read or alter sessions, including credentials.

  • TLS services refuse SSL, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 and weak cipher suites.
  • Certificates chain to the internal CA, match the host name and are in date.
  • LDAP, SQL and RDP sessions are encrypted wherever they carry credentials.

Record: host, port and protocol weaknesses; passing means current TLS only, with valid certificates.

items.title: SMB signing requirements
items.description:
Where SMB signing is not required, captured authentication can be relayed to that host. Domain controllers require it by default; other hosts often do not.

  • Every server, not just domain controllers, sets Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always).
  • Clients require signing for outbound connections.
  • Exceptions such as storage appliances and legacy devices are listed with a reason.

Record: hosts where signing is enabled but not required; passing means signing is required wherever supported.

items.title: LDAP signing and channel binding (network view)
items.description:
Unsigned LDAP binds, and LDAPS without channel binding, let relayed authentication reach the directory. Domain controller policy is confirmed in the Active Directory Security Review checklist.

  • Domain controllers refuse unsigned binds over plain LDAP, including simple binds.
  • LDAPS enforces channel binding.
  • Other LDAP services (appliances, non-Windows directories) are checked the same way.

Record: each directory server and its signing and channel binding state; passing means both are required.

items.title: LLMNR, NetBIOS name service and mDNS
items.description:
Link-local multicast name resolution, NetBIOS name service and mDNS let any host answer failed name lookups, so authentication can be captured or relayed.

  • Passive listening over a set period shows whether hosts send these queries.
  • LLMNR is disabled by policy and NetBIOS over TCP/IP is off where not needed.
  • Stale names (old file servers, mapped drives, typos) that trigger fallback lookups are noted.

Record: sources and names seen in fallback lookups; passing means no such traffic.

items.title: IPv6 router advertisements and DHCPv6
items.description:
Windows prefers IPv6 even on networks run as IPv4 only, so a host answering DHCPv6 or sending router advertisements can become clients' DNS server.

  • Passive listening shows whether hosts send DHCPv6 solicitations on IPv4-only segments.
  • Switches drop rogue router advertisements and DHCPv6 replies on user ports (RA Guard, DHCPv6 Guard or equivalent).
  • IPv6 is managed deliberately, or disabled or filtered where unused.

Record: segments with unmanaged IPv6 and whether rogue traffic is filtered; passing means managed or filtered.

items.title: WPAD and proxy auto-discovery
items.description:
Web Proxy Auto-Discovery lets clients fetch proxy settings automatically; if the name is not defined internally, another host on the network can supply them.

  • Clients do not detect proxy settings automatically unless WPAD is deliberately published.
  • Where WPAD is used, its DNS or DHCP entry exists and is served by the organisation.
  • No WPAD lookups fall through to LLMNR or NetBIOS name service.

Record: WPAD lookups observed and client proxy settings; passing means WPAD is disabled or authoritatively defined.

items.title: Authentication coercion and relay targets
items.description:
Finds services that accept relayed NTLM and hosts that can be made to authenticate elsewhere: the two halves of a relay path.

  • Web services accepting NTLM, such as certificate web enrolment, require HTTPS and Extended Protection for Authentication.
  • Print spooler and similar coercible services are off where unneeded.
  • Directory and certificate service detail is checked in the Active Directory Security Review checklist.

Record: relay targets and coercible hosts with the missing control; passing means no relay path reaches a privileged service.

items.title: Default and vendor credentials
items.description:
Vendor default accounts remain one of the commonest ways in. Use only low-rate, authorised attempts that cannot lock accounts.

  • Appliances, BMCs, printers, cameras, databases and admin consoles refuse vendor default or blank credentials.
  • Built-in accounts that cannot be removed are renamed or disabled where supported.
  • Attempts are limited to the documented defaults for each product.

Record: device, account and access gained, without passwords in the report body; passing means no default credential works.

items.title: Shared local administrator passwords
items.description:
One local administrator password on many hosts turns one compromised machine into many.

  • Local administrator passwords are unique per host and rotated (Windows LAPS or an equivalent).
  • A local credential recovered during authorised testing is checked for reuse on an agreed sample only.
  • Local accounts are denied network logon where not needed.
  • LAPS coverage from the directory is checked in the Active Directory Security Review checklist.

Record: account and number of hosts sharing it; passing means every local admin password is unique.

items.title: Credentials and sensitive data in file shares
items.description:
Over-permissive shares often hold passwords, keys and personal data readable by every domain user.

  • Shares readable or writable by Everyone, Authenticated Users or Domain Users are listed.
  • Readable files are reviewed for passwords, private keys, connection strings and password manager exports.
  • Writable shares holding software or scripts are flagged, as changes there run on other hosts.

Record: share path, permission and type of sensitive content, secrets redacted; passing means least privilege and no credentials found.

items.title: Credentials in scripts, deployment shares and configuration files
items.description:
Logon scripts, deployment shares and configuration files often hold service and admin passwords.

  • SYSVOL and NETLOGON scripts hold no usable passwords (Group Policy Preferences are covered in the Active Directory checklist).
  • Deployment shares, unattended answer files and imaging task sequences hold no reusable credentials.
  • Application configuration files do not hold database or service passwords in clear.

Record: location, credential type and owning account; passing means none found.

items.title: Password reuse and weak service passwords
items.description:
Checks whether credentials found during the test work elsewhere, which turns isolated findings into a chain.

  • Recovered credentials are tried only on an agreed sample of services, at a rate that cannot cause lockout.
  • Service and application accounts do not share passwords with user or admin accounts.
  • Any offline password assessment is authorised and its material handled securely (NIST SP 800-115 section 5.1).

Record: each reuse case with source and destination; passing means no credential works beyond its own system.

items.title: Database services exposure and authentication
items.description:
Databases hold the data most reports care about and are often reachable from user networks with weak authentication.

  • Database listeners (SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch) face application and admin zones only.
  • No database accepts anonymous, default or blank-password logins.
  • Authentication and data in transit are encrypted.

Record: instance, version, reachability and authentication mode; passing means restricted, authenticated and encrypted.

items.title: Database privileges and server-level features
items.description:
Database settings can turn database access into operating system or cross-server access.

  • Application accounts are not database administrators.
  • Features that run operating system commands or reach other servers, such as SQL Server xp_cmdshell and linked servers with stored credentials, are disabled or restricted.
  • Database service accounts are not domain or local administrators.

Record: instance, risky setting or privilege and account; passing means least privilege and no unneeded server-level features.

items.title: Virtualisation management planes
items.description:
Hypervisors and their management servers control every guest, so access to them equals control of the servers they host.

  • Hosts and management servers (for example vCenter, ESXi, Hyper-V) are reachable only from a management network.
  • They are patched against known exploited vulnerabilities and run no unneeded services.
  • Admin rights are not granted to broad directory groups, and root accounts are not shared.

Record: endpoints, versions, reachability and admin groups; passing means isolated, current and tightly administered.

items.title: Backup systems and repositories
items.description:
Backup platforms hold copies of everything and are the main recovery route after ransomware, so their compromise does double damage.

  • Backup consoles, agents and repositories face management sources only.
  • Backup administration uses separate accounts, not domain administrators, with MFA where offered.
  • At least one copy is immutable or offline, and repositories are not writable through open shares.

Record: components, reachability, admin model and immutability evidence; passing means isolated administration and a protected copy.

items.title: Storage management and network file systems
items.description:
Storage arrays and network file systems often trust the network rather than the user.

  • SAN and NAS management interfaces sit on the management network and refuse default credentials.
  • NFS exports are limited to named hosts and do not map remote root to local root.
  • iSCSI targets require authentication (CHAP or stronger) and sit on a dedicated network.

Record: device or export, setting and exposure; passing means storage is reachable and mountable only by intended hosts.

items.title: Network device management
items.description:
Switches, routers, firewalls and wireless controllers enforce segmentation, so their management must be tighter than anything they protect.

  • Management uses SSH or HTTPS from management addresses only; Telnet and HTTP are off.
  • Authentication is centralised (TACACS+ or RADIUS) with named accounts.
  • Legacy provisioning services such as Smart Install are disabled.
  • Configuration backups are not on open shares or TFTP.

Record: device, protocols, reachability and firmware; passing means encrypted, restricted, attributable management.

items.title: Printers and multifunction devices
items.description:
Multifunction devices store directory, email and scan-to-folder credentials and often keep vendor defaults.

  • The admin interface has a non-default password and uses HTTPS.
  • Stored LDAP, SMTP and SMB accounts are low privilege, and their passwords cannot be read back or sent to another server by changing settings.
  • Unneeded services (Telnet, FTP, SNMP write, Wi-Fi Direct) are off.

Record: device, firmware, settings and any credential exposure; passing means locked-down administration and least-privilege stored accounts.

items.title: Cameras, building systems, VoIP and other embedded devices
items.description:
Embedded devices are rarely patched and often sit on flat networks next to servers.

  • IP cameras, door controllers, building management, UPS, VoIP and OT devices are inventoried and segmented.
  • They refuse default credentials and run supported firmware.
  • Their management interfaces are unreachable from user networks.

Record: device type, network location, firmware and access obtained; passing means segmented, supported devices with unique credentials.

items.title: Network access control on wired ports
items.description:
Shows whether an unknown device in a wall port gets network access, the first step of any physical or insider scenario.

  • Ports in meeting rooms and public areas are tried with an unregistered device.
  • 802.1X is enforced; MAC authentication bypass is limited to devices that need it, in restricted VLANs.
  • Devices failing authentication land in a quarantine VLAN.
  • A device behind an authorised one (a phone pass-through port) does not inherit its access.

Record: port, outcome and VLAN assigned; passing means unknown devices get no internal access.

items.title: Endpoint protection observations
items.description:
Records how endpoint protection behaved during authorised testing, which shows the client what a real attacker would have met.

  • Endpoint protection or EDR is present on the hosts touched, and the test actions it blocked or alerted on are noted.
  • Tamper protection stops local administrators disabling it.
  • Servers and legacy systems without coverage are listed.

Record: host, product, action and response observed; passing means full coverage, with key actions blocked or alerted.

items.title: Logging and detection of test activity
items.description:
Checks whether the client saw the test, using their records rather than assumptions (NIST SP 800-115 section 3.2).

  • The client's monitoring team reports which test activities raised alerts and when.
  • Domain controller, firewall and key server logs are collected centrally and retained.
  • Scanning, failed and privileged logons and lateral movement are matched against alerts raised.

Record: a timeline of test actions against detections and response; passing means significant actions were detected and escalated.

items.title: Active Directory review (separate checklist)
items.description:
The directory itself is covered by the Active Directory Security Review checklist, so its checks are not repeated here.

  • That checklist is attached to this phase whenever a domain is in scope.
  • Network-level findings pass across to it: relay paths, shared local credentials and credentials found in SYSVOL.
  • Whether a domain account was supplied or obtained is noted, as it sets the depth of the directory review.

Record: the linked checklist and starting account; passing means directory coverage is tracked there.

phase_external_v2.name: External Infrastructure Review
phase_external_v2.description: Coverage tracker for an external, internet-facing test: ownership and authorisation, DNS, exposed services and known exploited vulnerabilities, remote access and admin interfaces, TLS, email security, web servers, CDN origins, exposed storage and code, public information, IPv6 and amplification. Tick each item once covered or recorded as not applicable, keeping the evidence each item names and validating every finding rather than taking it from a scanner.

items.title: Ownership of every in-scope address
items.description:
Confirms each address belongs to the client, or has written third-party permission, before active testing begins.

  • Each range is checked against regional internet registry records and the client's asset list.
  • Cloud and hosting addresses are confirmed as currently assigned to the client's account, as they are reallocated often.
  • Managed or shared platforms have the provider's permission or fall under its published testing policy.

Record: each range with ownership evidence and date checked; passing means no target lacks evidence.

items.title: Ownership of every in-scope domain and host name
items.description:
Domains and subdomains can point at third-party services, so each is tied to the client before it is tested.

  • Registrant and registrar details, or the client's written confirmation, cover each domain.
  • Each host name is resolved and its address checked against the confirmed ranges.
  • Names resolving to SaaS, CDN or shared hosting are tested only within that provider's rules.

Record: name, resolved address, owner and permission relied on; passing means every tested name maps to an authorised target.

items.title: External rules of engagement and source addresses
items.description:
Sets how the test runs, so the client can tell test traffic from a real attack and nothing disruptive happens by surprise.

  • Tester source addresses are given to the client, and whether testing goes through or around the WAF and IPS is recorded.
  • Denial of service, account lockout and high-rate testing are explicitly in or out of scope.
  • Testing windows and an emergency contact are agreed.

Record: source addresses, windows and exclusions; passing means the client can attribute all test traffic.

items.title: Asset discovery from public sources
items.description:
Finds forgotten internet-facing assets, using only sources the rules of engagement allow (NIST SP 800-115 section 5.2.1).

  • Certificate transparency logs, DNS data, search engines and registry records are searched for client names and domains.
  • Every find is reconciled with the agreed scope; out-of-scope finds are reported, not tested.
  • Forgotten assets (old campaigns, staging sites, acquired brands) are flagged.

Record: each asset, its source and scope status; passing means the client's inventory matches what is publicly visible.

items.title: DNS zone transfers
items.description:
A zone transfer open to anyone hands over the whole zone, including hosts that were never meant to be listed.

  • Each authoritative name server, including secondaries run by providers, refuses zone transfers to unauthorised hosts.
  • Transfers are limited to named secondaries, ideally with transaction signatures (TSIG).
  • Both the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of each name server are checked.

Record: name server, zone and result; passing means every server refuses the transfer.

items.title: Dangling DNS records and subdomain takeover conditions
items.description:
Records pointing at deleted cloud resources, expired domains or released addresses let others claim them and serve content under the client's name.

  • CNAMEs to cloud services (storage, app hosting, CDN, SaaS) resolve to resources the client still owns.
  • A and AAAA records do not point at released cloud addresses.
  • NS and MX records do not delegate to expired domains or unclaimed provider zones.

Record: record, target and evidence it is unclaimed, without claiming it; passing means every record resolves to a client-controlled resource.

items.title: Wildcard DNS records
items.description:
Wildcard records make every possible subdomain resolve, which hides real assets during discovery and can lend credibility to look-alike names.

  • Each zone is checked for wildcard A, AAAA or CNAME records and where they point.
  • The wildcard target is a controlled, hardened host, not a third-party service others can configure.
  • Discovery results are filtered for wildcard answers so real hosts are not missed.

Record: zone, wildcard target and purpose; passing means wildcards are absent, or deliberate and controlled.

items.title: Exposed DNS servers and resolver behaviour
items.description:
Authoritative servers that also resolve for anyone can be abused for amplification and reveal cached lookups.

  • Authoritative servers refuse recursion for external clients.
  • Version and host name queries disclose no software details.
  • DNSSEC, where deployed, validates correctly.
  • CAA records restrict which certificate authorities may issue for the domain.

Record: server, recursion result and disclosures; passing means no open resolver and no version disclosure.

items.title: Exposed service inventory against expectations
items.description:
Establishes exactly what is reachable from the internet (NIST SP 800-115 sections 4.1 and 4.2).

  • All 65,535 TCP ports are covered on every address.
  • UDP covers at least DNS, NTP, SNMP, IKE and SIP.
  • Services and versions are identified by protocol behaviour, not port.
  • Results are compared with the client's list of intended services; anything else is confirmed with the client.

Record: address, port, service, version and whether intended; passing means only intended services are exposed.

items.title: Versions against known exploited vulnerabilities
items.description:
Exposed software with a known exploited flaw is the likeliest way in, so versions are checked against vendor advisories and the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalogue.

  • Version evidence is direct (banner, protocol response, static assets); inferred versions are labelled.
  • KEV issues are confirmed by non-destructive checks only.
  • If a KEV-listed flaw was exposed, the client is asked whether it checked for compromise, not only patched.

Record: product, version, CVE and evidence; passing means no KEV-listed vulnerability is exposed.

items.title: Unsupported internet-facing software
items.description:
Software past vendor end of support cannot be fixed by patching and should not face the internet.

  • Operating systems, web servers, frameworks and VPN or firewall firmware are checked against vendor support dates.
  • Appliances report firmware versions that are still supported.
  • Any unsupported component has a dated replacement plan.

Record: component, version and end-of-support date; passing means everything exposed is supported.

items.title: Remote access gateways
items.description:
VPN, virtual desktop and remote desktop gateways are prime targets and appear often in the KEV catalogue.

  • The product and exact version are identified and checked against vendor advisories.
  • Pre-authentication pages expose no version detail, internal host names or user lists.
  • Legacy protocols, weak TLS and IKE aggressive mode with pre-shared keys are not offered.

Record: gateway, version, protocols and pre-authentication exposure; passing means current, supported and a minimal pre-authentication surface.

items.title: Remote access authentication
items.description:
A remote access service is only as strong as how it authenticates users before granting network access.

  • MFA is enforced for every user, including contractors and break-glass accounts, with no legacy or fallback path that skips it.
  • Error messages and timing do not reveal which usernames are valid.
  • Certificate or device posture checks, where claimed, are actually enforced.

Record: methods offered, MFA behaviour and enumeration results; passing means every path requires MFA and gives nothing away about accounts.

items.title: Administrative interfaces on the internet
items.description:
Management interfaces for firewalls, routers, hypervisors, storage, BMCs and applications should not be reachable from the internet.

  • No device management page, SSH, Telnet or SNMP service answers untrusted addresses.
  • Application admin paths (CMS, application server and database consoles) are restricted by source or unpublished.
  • Any exposure the client calls necessary has MFA and source restriction.

Record: address, interface and product; passing means management is reachable only through a VPN or from fixed admin addresses.

items.title: Remote desktop, SSH and file services exposed directly
items.description:
Directly exposed RDP, SSH, SMB and file transfer services invite password guessing and exploitation of protocol flaws.

  • RDP and SMB are not exposed to the internet.
  • SSH, where needed, uses key authentication, refuses root and password logins and offers current algorithms.
  • File transfer services refuse anonymous access and do not run FTP without TLS.

Record: service, address and configuration; passing means only justified, hardened services, preferably behind a VPN.

items.title: Databases, caches and search services exposed directly
items.description:
Data services reachable from the internet are a frequent cause of bulk data exposure.

  • SQL Server, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch and similar do not answer untrusted addresses.
  • Where reachable, none accepts unauthenticated or default logins; confirm without reading more data than proves the point.
  • Message queues and container management APIs are not exposed.

Record: service, version and authentication result; passing means none are exposed.

items.title: Default and weak credentials on exposed services
items.description:
Checks whether exposed logins accept vendor defaults or trivially weak passwords, at a rate the rules of engagement allow.

  • Only documented vendor defaults and a small agreed list are tried, never broad guessing.
  • Attempts stay below lockout thresholds and avoid busy periods.
  • Any successful login stops at proof of access and is reported to the client promptly.

Record: service, account and outcome, with no passwords in the report body; passing means no default or weak credential works.

items.title: Rate limiting and lockout on public authentication
items.description:
Public logins without throttling allow password spraying and credential stuffing at scale.

  • Repeated failures trigger throttling, delay, a challenge or lockout, without letting outsiders lock out named users at will.
  • Limits apply per account and per source, and cannot be sidestepped through other endpoints such as legacy protocols or mobile APIs.
  • Responses are identical for valid and invalid usernames.

Record: endpoint, threshold observed and enumeration result; passing means every authentication path is throttled.

items.title: TLS protocol versions and cipher suites
items.description:
Weak TLS settings allow downgrade or decryption of traffic to public services.

  • SSL 2.0, SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are disabled on every TLS service, including mail and VPN.
  • TLS 1.2 offers only forward-secret AEAD cipher suites, and TLS 1.3 is enabled.
  • Insecure renegotiation and TLS compression are disabled.

Record: host, port, protocols and weak suites accepted; passing means TLS 1.2 or later with strong suites only.

items.title: Certificates and HTTPS enforcement
items.description:
Certificate faults break trust and train users to click through warnings.

  • Certificates match host names, chain to a public root, are in date and use strong keys and signatures.
  • Certificates near expiry are noted and monitoring of expiry is confirmed.
  • HTTP redirects to HTTPS, and HTTP Strict Transport Security is set on web services.

Record: host, issuer, expiry and faults; passing means valid certificates everywhere and HTTPS enforced.

items.title: SPF records
items.description:
SPF lists the servers allowed to send mail for a domain; a weak record lets others send as the client.

  • Each sending domain has exactly one SPF record ending in a fail (-all) or soft fail (~all) qualifier, never +all or ?all.
  • The record stays within the 10 DNS lookup limit and names only services still in use.
  • Domains that send no mail publish a record authorising nobody.

Record: domain, record and faults; passing means one current, strict record per domain.

items.title: DKIM signing
items.description:
DKIM signs outgoing mail so receivers can verify it was not forged or altered.
